title: Set app.set('trust proxy', 1) so rate-limit buckets are per-client instead of site-wide
description: index.js has no trust-proxy setting (verified: zero 'app.set(' calls), so behind Caddy every express-rate-limit bucket keys on the proxy address and is GLOBAL. submissionLimiter is 10/min SITE-WIDE (index.js:279), evidenceLimiter 30/min (281), generalLimiter 60/min (282). One noisy client can rate-limit every real customer, and any mutating smoke run against prod burns a tenth of the submission budget for that minute -- which is why 05-scripts/smoke-evidence.sh refuses to target production. Fix: app.set('trust proxy', 1) since exactly one proxy (Caddy) sits in front, then re-verify the limiters key on the real client IP.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #35 (security-reviewed, no HIGH/MEDIUM findings) and deployed. app.set('trust proxy', 1) added: all four express-rate-limit buckets now key on the real client instead of collapsing into one site-wide counter (submission 10/min, analysis 5/min, evidence 30/min, general 60/min were all global). Chose the integer 1 over true because true takes the LEFTMOST X-Forwarded-For entry, which is attacker-supplied, letting anyone mint a fresh bucket per request and bypass every limiter; 1 counts one hop from the right, the value Caddy appended. Verified exactly one hop: Caddy reverse_proxy -> 127.0.0.1:8089, container on loopback only, no CDN. New __tests__/trust-proxy.test.js (6 tests) proves per-client scoping, that a spoofed prefix is ignored, that one client cannot lock out another, and that rotating the header does not escape the limit -- plus regression guards that fail if anyone sets true or removes the setting. Suite 177/177. /security-review also confirmed no X-Forwarded-Host/Proto consumers exist, so trust proxy opens no host-injection path.

title: Bring test.diagnosticpro.io backend in sync with production evidence API

acceptance_criteria: test.diagnosticpro.io accepts the same work-order/document route and formats as production; a non-payment upload/list/delete smoke test passes; frontend and backend revisions are traceable.
notes:
Observed 2026-08-01 after production deploy b155736; POST /evidence/diag_.../document returned 404 Cannot POST on test.diagnosticpro.io.
ROOT CAUSE (verified): diagnosticpro-backend-test was created by hand 2026-07-23, is NOT in docker-compose.yml (empty com.docker.compose.project.config_files label), and the VPS deploy runs 'docker compose up -d --build' which manages only the 'backend' service. Nothing has ever updated it, so it is frozen on pre-document-evidence code -> POST /evidence/:id/document 404 on test, 400 on prod. Frontend is already in sync (Caddy test block serves the same /srv/diagnosticpro/dist and its @api matcher already includes /evidence*); only the backend container is stale.

ADVERSARIAL CLAIM REFUTED BY EXPERIMENT: a 9-agent review asserted that adding a second compose service risks leaving the PROD container created-but-never-started (8089 unbound, 502, no self-heal) if the new service fails at create. Reproduced on a throwaway project on BOTH the dev box (compose v5.0.1) and the VPS itself (v5.1.3), including the case where prod's own config changes and compose logs 'Recreate': the collision aborts the converge BEFORE prod is touched. Prod kept the same container id, stayed running, kept its old config; a follow-up 'up -d' healed cleanly. Real failure mode is milder: compose exits 1, 'set -euo pipefail' aborts the deploy script, so the frontend build/rsync are skipped and prod keeps serving old code. Visible (red deploy), recoverable, NOT an outage. The proposed production deploy-script patch is therefore not required as a blocker fix.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live (PRs #32 + #33).

ROOT CAUSE: diagnosticpro-backend-test was created by hand 2026-07-23 with an EMPTY com.docker.compose.project.config_files label and no entry in docker-compose.yml, so the deploy's 'docker compose up -d --build' (which only knew about 'backend') could never see, adopt or replace it. It sat on a superseded image id for three weeks. Frontend was already in sync; only the backend container was stale.

FIX: backend-test is now a first-class unprofiled compose service on prod's exact image tag (no second build), own diagnosticpro-test-data volume, env_file .env.test with required:false. GIT_SHA threaded build-arg -> Dockerfile ARG -> /healthz .gitSha. Blocking test-surface-parity job in deploy.yml so this cannot silently drift again.

ACCEPTANCE:
AC#1 same route/formats as prod - POST /evidence/PROBE/document returns 400 application/json on BOTH hosts (test was 404).
AC#2 non-payment upload/list/delete smoke - 05-scripts/smoke-evidence.sh against https://test.diagnosticpro.io: submission created -> document attached -> listed back -> wrong token rejected 401 -> deleted 204 -> 0 rows remain. PASS.
AC#3 revision traceability - git main / prod healthz / test healthz all report 57411df59558.

Secret boundary intact: diagnosticpro-backend sk_live_..., diagnosticpro-backend-test sk_test_..., separate volumes. Both compose-managed and healthy.

NOTE: the parity gate failed on its first real run against a healthy surface - 'read < <(curl)' returns non-zero at EOF because curl -w emits no trailing newline, and set -e killed the step. Fixed in #33 with command substitution; gate now green. A check that cries wolf is worse than no check.

Collision risk was measured, not assumed: with the old container present, 'docker compose up -d' exits 1 and aborts BEFORE touching the running prod container (reproduced on the dev box AND the VPS at compose v5.1.3, including the Recreate case). The stale container was therefore removed on the host first, volume preserved.

title: Make the first screen answer the question on a phone
description: Most customers open the report on a phone within minutes of paying, and the first thing they want is: what is probably wrong, and what should I do. Today that is buried in document structure. Requirements: the headline cause and its confidence number visible without scrolling; a scannable section index; type legible at phone width without pinch-zoom; the price range reachable in one jump. This is the 'was that $4.99 worth it' moment and it is decided in about five seconds. Depends on the renderer decision.

title: Make the printed report work at a shop counter
description: Print is the real use: the customer prints it and carries it in. Requirements: no critical content split across a page break; the questions-to-ask section usable as a single standalone page the customer can hand over or hold; ink-economical (no full-bleed dark fills); legible at arm's length on a counter; page numbers and a per-page identifier so loose pages are reassemblable. Test by actually printing one, not by viewing it zoomed out. Depends on the renderer decision.

title: Decide whether to stay on pdfkit or move to an HTML-to-PDF renderer
description: Architecture decision, blocking the build work. pdfkit draws imperatively -- every layout change is code, page breaks are manual, and rich layout is expensive to express. The alternative is rendering HTML/CSS to PDF (Playwright/Chromium is already a dependency of the e2e suite, or a library like weasyprint). Trade-offs to weigh with evidence, not preference: layout expressiveness, print fidelity and page-break control (CSS has real page-break primitives; pdfkit does not), image weight, cold-start and per-report generation time, container size (the image already carries texlive and poppler), determinism of output, and how much of reportPdfProduction.js survives. Note there is ALSO a reportWhiteglove.js path plus a latex/ directory -- establish which of the three is actually canonical before choosing. Deliverable: a decision record with the measured generation time for each option on a real report.

title: Research how comparable paid one-off reports are designed, and pick a direction
description: Design study, no code. Look at how other paid single-artifact reports handle the same job: home-inspection reports, vehicle history reports (Carfax/AutoCheck), medical lab results, independent lab test reports, and paid research/analyst notes. All share our constraint -- one document, read once under mild stress, sometimes printed, must feel worth the money. Capture: cover-page treatment, how the headline answer is surfaced, use of colour vs ink economy, how confidence/uncertainty is shown visually, table and callout patterns, and how they handle a section the reader may skip. Deliverable: 3 candidate directions with visual references and a recommendation, plus the one thing each does that we should steal. Constraint: it must be expressible in pdfkit, or the alternative must be named explicitly.

title: Redesign the diagnostic report PDF so it feels worth paying for
description:
The report content is right but the artifact looks plain. It is the ONLY thing a customer receives for their money -- the entire product experience after checkout is this one file -- so its design carries the perceived value of the whole purchase, and right now it undersells it.

Three distinct consumption contexts, each with different constraints, and the current PDF is tuned for none of them:
1. IMMEDIATE ON-SCREEN read, usually on a phone, minutes after paying. Needs scannable hierarchy, an answer visible without scrolling, and legible type at phone width.
2. PRINTED and carried into the shop. This is the actual use -- the report exists to be used at a counter. Needs page-break discipline, no critical content split across pages, ink-economical, and the questions section usable as a standalone page.
3. EMAILED later. No email infrastructure exists yet (see child bead) -- design decisions should not block it.

Current stack: pdfkit with IBM Plex Mono, in 02-src/backend/services/backend/reportPdfProduction.js (PDFValidationSystem, TypographyManager, DiagnosticPDFGenerator) plus a reportWhiteglove.js variant. Any redesign must survive the existing 15-section parse contract and must not rename the internal JSON keys, which are persisted in the analyses table.

RESEARCH FIRST, BUILD SECOND. This epic starts with a design study, not a code change.

The shipped prompt instead uses equipment-class-specific personas (Class 8 gets J1939 SPN/FMI and FMCSA out-of-service criteria; RV gets chassis-vs-house triage), which is good but different. Two options: (a) build the protocol into promptV3.js so the claim becomes true and becomes a real differentiator, or (b) stop describing it as a property of the live product. title: Rename the SHOP INTERROGATION and RIPOFF DETECTION report sections
description: promptV3.js and index.js both generate customer-facing report sections named 'SHOP INTERROGATION - 5 technical questions to expose incompetence' and 'RIPOFF DETECTION - parts cannon indicators'. Verified present in both files. The product's own CONVERSATION SCRIPTING section takes the opposite posture (informed, curious, explicitly tells the customer never to say 'my AI report says'), so the framing is inconsistent with the product's own guidance. Risk: a customer screenshots a report containing 'expose incompetence' and it reads as anti-mechanic -- alienating shop owners, who are themselves customers. Also a live trap for teammates mining reports for social content. Proposal: keep the substance, rename to something like 'QUESTIONS FOR YOUR SHOP' and 'COMMON OVERCHARGES'. Found 2026-08-13 during marketing positioning work.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #34, deployed and verified live. Renamed customer-facing headings '4. SHOP INTERROGATION' -> '4. QUESTIONS FOR YOUR SHOP' and '7. RIPOFF DETECTION' -> '7. title: Decide whether to run the backend on Node 22 so PDF extraction stops using the degraded fallback
description: Found 2026-08-09 while fixing CI. evidence/documents.js extracts PDF text via pdf-parse (pdf.js) and falls back to the pdftotext binary when that throws. pdf.js calls Promise.withResolvers, which does not exist until Node 22. The production Dockerfile pins node:20-slim, so PRODUCTION NEVER USES THE PURE-JS PATH -- every uploaded PDF work order is extracted by shelling out to pdftotext. It works (the Dockerfile does install poppler-utils) but it is slower, loses the pdf-parse page-delimiter handling that the OCR heuristic depends on, and nothing surfaces the degradation. Reproduced: docker run node:20-slim -> withResolvers undefined, 2 documents.test.js failures; same image + poppler-utils -> 5 passed. Options: (a) bump Dockerfile + engines to node:22-slim and keep poppler as fallback, (b) accept the fallback and document it as the intended path. (a) is deploy-affecting -- own PR, own smoke test. Relates to dpro-7gi (OCR scanned PDFs).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #31 (squash 963b959), deployed and verified in production. Backend moved node:20-slim -> node:24-slim; engines >=22 (true floor). Chose 24 over 22: both pass 171/171, 24 is Active LTS to 2028-04-30 vs 2027-04-30. Node 20 was EOL 2026-04-30 -- prod had been unpatched 3 months. Verified in the live container: node v24.19.0, withResolvers present, extractDocumentText -> parser 'pdf-text' (was 'pdftotext'). healthz ok, homepage 200. Also fixed: no .dockerignore meant COPY . . clobbered the builder's node_modules and baked /app/.env + a 113-row diagnosticpro.db into any locally built image.

title: Establish email delivery for reports
description: NOTE, correcting a working assumption: DiagnosticPro DOES have a database -- SQLite via better-sqlite3 at /data/diagnosticpro.db, holding diagnostic_submissions, analyses, evidence and whop_users. There is no Postgres and none is needed at current volume. What is genuinely missing is EMAIL: no ESP is connected, brand/stack.md records the gap, and an emailLogs concept exists in legacy Firestore notes but nothing sends. Scope: pick a sending provider that fits the self-host posture, decide attachment-vs-link delivery (a link keeps the PDF behind the existing evidence-token auth and lets us fix a bad report after send; an attachment survives a dead link), handle bounces, and honour the fact that report URLs are currently signed/tokenised. Deliberately AFTER the redesign -- do not let email constrain the layout work. Deferred until a provider is chosen.
notes:
Deliberately after the redesign. No ESP is connected and none is chosen; letting email delivery constrain the layout work would be backwards. Revive when a sending provider is picked.
TRIGGER SET 2026-08-14 (Jeremy): 'hold off on email til we actually have a customer.' Revive on the FIRST PAYING CUSTOMER, not on a vendor decision -- picking an ESP before anyone has bought is optimizing a step nobody has reached.

Why this is safe to defer: report delivery ALREADY WORKS without email. The customer polls the Report page and downloads the PDF, and Stripe sends the payment receipt. Email is an experience improvement, not a gap in the product, so nothing is blocked.

Decision context captured while it is fresh, so the next session does not re-litigate it:
- MXroute CAN send (it is SMTP) but should not be the transactional path. It sells mailboxes on shared IPs, its AUP is not written for app-generated mail, and -- the deciding reason -- SMTP only confirms the handoff. It gives no bounce or complaint webhooks, so the actual paid deliverable would be sent blind, with a complaining customer as the only bounce detector.
- Split by purpose when the time comes: MXroute keeps human mail (replies, support, one-to-one); a dedicated transactional sender does report delivery.
- Resend is the likely pick (best DX, free tier covers early volume). Postmark is stronger on pure transactional deliverability if that ever matters. SES is cheapest at scale but you own warmup/reputation and it adds an AWS dependency to an estate that just exited GCP.
- Do NOT self-host this. Email deliverability is the one place the self-host posture is actively wrong -- a fresh IP sending transactional mail gets filtered, and fixing that is permanent part-time work.
- Open sub-decision: attachment vs link. Recommend LINK -- it reuses the existing evidence-token auth and the /view/:submissionId signed-URL route, keeps the message light for deliverability, and lets a bad report be regenerated after send. Watch link expiry for someone opening it weeks later.
